title: NCEP captured 12-43% of buoy stress strengthening at 19 tropical sites in 2023-2025
abstract: At 19 fixed tropical buoy sites, we compared NCEP R1 and R2 surface stress and latent heat flux in February 2023-December 2025 with 2010-2019. With equal calendar-month weights, buoy along-direction stress rose by 0.01040 N m-2. R1 rose by 0.00449 and R2 by 0.00121, or 43% and 12% of the buoy rise. Season-adjusted stress-error changes were -0.00613 and -0.00926 N m-2, with conditional 95 percent block intervals below zero. After pre-2020 response calibration, R2 retained a negative change of -0.00677 [-0.01160, -0.00156], while the R1 interval included zero. R2 raw changes passed both alternate baseline checks; calibrated inference was weaker with a 2015-2019 baseline. Cross-direction intervals included zero. Stress accuracy fell while absolute heat-flux accuracy rose, although heat-flux error changes remained large and negative. Pacific sites carried most of the stress change; Atlantic sites had larger heat changes. This extends recent NCEP surface-field checks to momentum forcing. It does not show that SST input error caused the stress change. Sparse coverage, bulk-flux error, shared assimilated observations, fixed calibration and tropical scope limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, hashes and an independent numerical audit are included.
